name: Visa-free entry
summary: EU citizens and citizens of many listed countries enter visa-free, up to 90 days. Holders of a valid Schengen visa or listed residence permits can stay up to 30 days. Some countries get 30 days under bilateral deals.

other: Stay is up to 90 days in any 180 days.
Check the official page for the full country list.

name: Short-stay visa (visa C)
summary: For transit or stays up to 90 days in any 180 days. Single or multiple entry. Multiple-entry visas run from 6 months to 5 years.

savings.note: At least 50 EUR per day of the requested stay

processing: Decision due in 10 days, up to 30 or 60 days if more documents are needed.

name: Long-stay visa (visa D)
summary: For stays over 90 days and up to 180 days within a year. Covers work or business and digital nomads. Visa D holders who want to work must apply for residence and a work permit within ten days of getting the visa.

name: Digital nomad temporary residence
summary: For people working remotely for a foreign employer or their own company registered outside Montenegro. First permit up to two years, extendable up to two more.

other: Proof of financial means (amount not stated on the page).
Proof of accommodation and health insurance.
Proof of remote work, like a contract with a foreign company.
Clean record: no unconditional sentence over 6 months.
Passport valid 3 months past the stay.
Page is older and mentions a draft law, so check current rules.

stay.note: Extension up to two more years, apply at least 30 days before expiry.

processing: Permit within 40 days of a proper application, per the page.
steps: Apply in person at the Ministry of Internal Affairs where you live.
Officer fills the form and takes photo, two fingerprints and signature.
Get a certificate confirming the request.
Collect the permit from the local MIA unit.

name: Temporary residence (general rules)
summary: Temporary residence is granted for family reunification, study, work, property ownership, humanitarian reasons and research. General permits last up to one year. You need funds, accommodation and health insurance.

other: Sufficient funds, accommodation and health insurance.
Passport valid at least 3 months beyond the stay.

name: Temporary residence and work permit (employment)
summary: Foreigners need a combined residence and work permit. You can only work for the employer named in the permit. Up to one year, extendable to two years in total.

name: Seasonal work permit
summary: Up to six months, extendable by two months, with a cap of eight months in a year.

stay.note: Cap of 8 months in a year.

name: Intra-company transfer and agreed services permit
summary: For posted workers and agreed services. Up to one year, extendable to two years.

name: Temporary residence for study
summary: Needs a school enrollment certificate. Students can work up to 15 hours a week.

name: Family reunification
summary: For close family of a Montenegrin national or a foreigner with temporary or permanent residence. Permits last up to one year.

name: Temporary residence for property owners
summary: Available for owners of real estate in Montenegro, backed by a land registry extract or other ownership proof. No investment minimum was found in the law text read.

other: Check current rules and any amount with the Ministry of Interior.

name: Humanitarian temporary residence
summary: For trafficking or domestic violence victims, certain minors and other justified humanitarian reasons. Up to one year and extendable. Asylum is a separate process, so check the official page.

name: Permanent residence
summary: After five years of uninterrupted legal residence. You need funds, health insurance, housing and basic Montenegrin. The card is valid five years and renewable.

eligibility.language: Basic Montenegrin, tested. Not needed over 65.
other: Five years of uninterrupted legal residence. Study time counts half.
Absences up to 10 months total, or a single one up to 6 months.
Stable, sufficient funds, health insurance and housing.

name: Citizenship by marriage (admittance)
summary: Married to a Montenegrin national for at least 3 years and holding permanent residence. Other conditions apply.

other: Articles 8 and 9 conditions were not listed on the page.

name: Citizenship by descent
summary: Children with Montenegrin parents get citizenship. A child with one Montenegrin parent and one foreign parent can apply before turning 23.

citizenship.note: Adults who hold another nationality generally lose Montenegrin nationality, except if acquired before 3 June 2006.

name: Citizenship for emigrants and their descendants
summary: A Montenegrin emigrant and third-degree direct-line relatives can be admitted after 2 years of legal continuous residence in Montenegro.
